# Get-ZbxTrend

## SYNOPSIS

Gets the hourly trends of items.

## SYNTAX

```
Get-ZbxTrend [[-Item] <ZabbixReference<ZabbixItem>[]>] [-From <DateTimeOffset>] [-Till <DateTimeOffset>] [-Limit <int>] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The Get-ZbxTrend cmdlet reads trends with trend.get: for each hour, the minimum, average and maximum of an item's numeric values and how many there were, which the server keeps after the raw history ages out. It selects by item (-Item: names, ids or piped items) and by time (-From and -Till), at most -Limit records; trends have no -Filter. It writes ZabbixTrendRecord objects and needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Get a day of an item's trends

```powershell
Get-ZbxItem -Host 'web-01' -Name 'Requests' | Get-ZbxTrend -From (Get-Date).AddDays(-1) |
    Select-Object @{ n = 'Hour'; e = { $_.Time } }, ValueMin, ValueAverage, ValueMax
```

A piped item binds -Item by its ItemId; -From takes a date, Unix seconds or a clock. An hour's trend appears once the hour ends.

### Example 2: Get the last week's peak of every item of a host

```powershell
Get-ZbxItem -Host 'web-01' | Get-ZbxTrend -From (Get-Date).AddDays(-7) |
    Group-Object ItemId | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject]@{ ItemId = $_.Name; Peak = ($_.Group.ValueMax | Measure-Object -Maximum).Maximum } }
```

Group the hourly records by item and keep the highest maximum.

## INPUTS

- `ZabbixReference<ZabbixItem>[]`: Bound to -Item (ByPropertyName). Represents a reference to an API object: a parameter that points at an API object takes its id, its name, or the object itself piped from a Get- cmdlet, and becomes an id before the call — one parameter, three spellings, one resolution.
